newsitem.title: USA: DuPont Merck urges caution on Warfarin.
newsitem.headline: DuPont Merck urges caution on Warfarin.

text.p: DuPont Merck on Wednesday urged patients to be cautious in switching from its formulation of a blood-thinning product to a generic version by Barr Laboratories approved earlier in the day by the Food and Drug Administration.
DuPont Merck called its product, Coumadin, or Warfarin Sodium tablets, a complex drug and said in a release that patients should not be switched from its formulation to Barr's without consultation.
Barr shares closed up 4-5/8 Wednesday at 36-1/2 after its announcement that the FDA had approved its generic version of the blood-thinner.
DuPont Merck is co-owned by DuPont Co and Merck and Co Inc. DuPont shares closed down two on Wednesday at 109-7/8, and Merck shares closed unchanged at 90-7/8.
Merck said in a release that it continues to believe the FDA should use more stringent standards in determining the benefits and risks of such drugs.
